cefrAlignment: C1: the lesson asks learners to build a reasoned argument with a criterion, a concession and a qualified verdict, which matches the CEFR C1 descriptors for spoken production (developing an argument systematically, with relevant supporting detail and qualifications) and goes beyond the B2/C1 'weigh both sides' taught in Abstract discussion.
examFidelity: IELTS Part 3 (no preparation, 60 s timer) and TOEFL Take an Interview (no preparation, 45 s) match exams.ts; the band 7 Fluency and Coherence quote ('Flexible use of spoken discourse markers, connectives and cohesive features') is verbatim from the public descriptors.
fixes: Trimmed the Part 3 model (ex4) from 143 to 135 words so it fits 60 s at a natural pace, and rewrote an awkwardly placed trailing clause ('…if you have to book months ahead') as a clear concession
openConcerns: Speak tasks are self-assessed only; learners may over-rate how 'decisive' their verdicts sound without teacher feedback
learnerOutcome: A learner can answer 'How far do you agree…?' and 'Is it fair…?' questions with a calibrated position, a named criterion, a real concession and a justified verdict instead of a list of pros and cons.
